title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1970-06-24
source: center lodge, mics mounted on rails->120-min. Sony cassette audience master-> analog cassette XL II, no dolby->Sony TC D5M DAT->playback on Sony PCM R-700-> HDD via za2->CDR master via CD Architect->EAC->Sound Forge->SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent audience recording of a legendary show featuring a smoking Dark Star and St. Stephen, captured with surprisingly good clarity for the era.
ai_review.review: Fans rave about this performance, calling the Ken‑Mark‑Jim version of Dark Star and the St. Stephen run “unreal,” and praising Phil’s thunderous Not Fade Away. The audience tape is noted as a solid, clear capture given the scarcity of soundboard sources from mid‑1970, making it a prized relic for Deadheads.

ai_rating.rationale: All six reviews are strongly positive (4–5 stars), repeatedly highlighting standout songs and noting the recording is good despite being an audience source; consistency across multiple detailed comments yields high confidence.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers describe the tape as a "good recording" with enough clarity to enjoy the performance, though they note the general lack of soundboard tapes from this era.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Described as "the set" and a timeless, powerful show; transitions and jams are praised for their energy and cohesion.

band_member_comments.Phil: Banging away on Not Fade Away (NFA) – highlighted for his driving bass work.
